# Mèngpó: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Mèngpó** is what the evidence put back.

Mèngpó's myth is a single scene, retold for centuries: the old woman, the bridge, the bowl — the gentlest moment in the whole machinery of the afterlife. Chinese folk cosmology orders the underworld like an administration: Yánluó's ten courts judge the deeds of the life, assign the punishments and the repayments — and then send the soul to Mèngpó.  At the Nàihé Bridge she ladles her tea of five flavors; the soul drinks, and the record of the life — the loves, the hatreds, the unfinished business — dissolves.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Mèngpó
- **ASCII form:** mengpo
- **Meaning:** "'Old Lady Meng' (孟婆), the goddess who brews the tea of forgetfulness"
- **Domain of influence:** Forgetting, Passage, Tea
- **Pantheon:** Chinese
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** —
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 150 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Mèngpó** to *mengpo* and 2 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **e → è** — Grave: falling (4th) tone: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.
- **o → ó** — Stress mark (acute/tone): the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Mèngpó** lives at [/sites/mengpo/](/sites/mengpo/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/mengpo/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/mengpo/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/mengpo/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Mèngpó** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Funerary & Memorial Services** — The last station before rebirth; the underworld’s own memorial rite.
- **Mental Health & Emotional Wellness** — The mercy of forgetting; the folk answer to grief and trauma.
- **Yoga, Meditation & Holistic Wellness** — Letting go as healing; the tea of release at the bridge.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Chinese tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Tao Te Ching](/texts/tao-te-ching/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/mengpo/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
